raw_case_text:
An 11-year-old male child presented to our hospital with a mass on the nasal aspect of the right eye that has been there for the last 2 years. It was associated with redness over the lesion which was relieved on topical medications. There was no associated pain, lacrimation, or photophobia. It has been associated with binocular diplopia on levoversion for the last 4 months. There was no history of a sudden increase in the size of the mass, pain, forward protrusion of the eyeball, or diminution of vision.
On systemic examination, no abnormality was detected. On ocular examination, the best corrected visual acuity was 6/6 in both eyes. His anterior segment and fundus examination was normal. Extraocular movements were decreased in the right eye on levoversion, levoelevation, and levodepression. Exophthalmometry using Hertel's exophthalmometer with interlateral canthal distance of 100 mm read 15 mm in both eyes.
Local examination revealed a bluish mass with irregular surface and ill-defined margins located in the medial rectus muscle. The mass became more prominent on dextroversion. The mass was 10 x 20 mm in size, firm, nodular, nontender, nonpulsatile, noncompressible, and nonreducible (Figure 1).
USG B-scan revealed a heterogenous mass approximately 23 x 13 mm in extraconal compartment close to the insertion of the medial rectus (MR) muscle with few hyperechoic flecks (Figure 2). MRI of the orbit revealed a well-defined mass of approximately 23 x 13 mm along the medial rectus (MR) muscle. It was isointense on T1W and hyperintense on T2W images with very minimal contrast enhancement (Figure 3). The patient initially consulted a local ophthalmic surgeon elsewhere, where it was initially diagnosed as cysticercosis and treated with albendazole and oral steroids.
A provisional diagnosis of hemangioma or lymphangioma with intralesional haemorrhage was made. As the patient had already received a course of oral steroids without any response and there was no evidence of active flow in the lesion, a decision to carry out excision biopsy was taken.
During surgical excision, the mass was found to be encapsulated by MR fibres. The MR fibres were separated and the mass was removed completely. The MR fibres were sutured together with 6-0 vicryl suture. The mass measuring 20 x 8 x 6.5 mm was removed and sent for histopathology. The histopathological examination revealed an intramuscular cavernous hemangioma (Figure 4). The patient was started on oral steroids for two weeks to ameliorate the postoperative edema and fibrosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 11-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of a mass on the nasal aspect of his right eye and a 4-month history of binocular diplopia on leftward gaze.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had a painless mass over the nasal aspect of his right eye for 2 years, associated with intermittent overlying redness relieved by topical eye drops, and developed binocular diplopia on levoversion 4 months prior to presentation. There was no sudden growth, pain, lacrimation, photophobia, proptosis, or visual loss. An outside ophthalmologist had previously diagnosed the lesion as ocular cysticercosis and treated him with oral albendazole and corticosteroids without improvement.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously treated elsewhere with oral albendazole and oral corticosteroids for presumed ocular myocysticercosis without response.
subjective.review_of_systems: Negative for ocular pain, tearing, photophobia, proptosis, or decreased visual acuity.

objective.physical_examination: Systemic examination was normal. Best-corrected visual acuity was 6/6 in both eyes, anterior segment and fundus examinations were normal, and Hertel exophthalmometry was 15 mm bilaterally (base 100 mm). Right extraocular motility was restricted in levoversion, levoelevation, and levodepression. Local ocular exam revealed a firm, nodular, nontender, nonpulsatile, noncompressible, nonreducible 10 x 20 mm bluish mass with ill-defined margins located in the right medial rectus muscle, becoming more prominent on dextroversion.
objective.routine_investigations: B-scan ocular ultrasonography showed a heterogeneous 23 x 13 mm extraconal mass near the insertion of the right medial rectus muscle containing a few hyperechoic flecks and no active internal blood flow.
objective.advanced_workup: Orbital MRI revealed a well-defined 23 x 13 mm mass along the right medial rectus muscle that was isointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and showed minimal post-contrast enhancement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Complete surgical excision of the 20 x 8 x 6.5 mm mass encapsulated within the right medial rectus muscle fibers was performed, and histopathology confirmed an intramuscular cavernous hemangioma of the medial rectus muscle, ruling out ocular myocysticercosis. Postoperatively, he received a 2-week course of oral corticosteroids to reduce edema and fibrosis.
